title: mRNA cap formation by the human respiratory syncytial virus large protein.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read the open-access full text (83 KB of body text) including the data availability statement, full methods and all figure legends; extracted every mutation identifier mentioned anywhere in the text (about 25 single-residue L-protein mutants plus 3 RNA-template mutants). Searched Europe PMC text-mined accessions, NCBI links and a Zenodo/Dryad DOI search: no deposited dataset exists. Attempted the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles download twice; it timed out both times, so the supplement itself is not retrievable here.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the supplement is Supplementary Figs S1-S6 plus supplementary results/discussion (i.e. gel images and bar graphs, not tables) comes from the supplementary captions in the article text, not from opening the file. Quantified activity values exist only as bar graphs inside figures, per the figure legends.

a1_downloadable.note: Data availability says only 'available in the article and in its online supplementary material' - no repository deposit. The three PDB entries cited (6U1X, 6PZK, 8FU3) are other groups' structures, and the two GenBank accessions (AAX23990, AAX23996) are the expression-construct sequences, not data. Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI returned nothing; the Europe PMC supplement endpoint timed out twice.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The outcome (relative capping activity, intermediate formation, methylation order) exists only as autoradiogram bands and bar graphs inside figures. A label column would have to be constructed by reading numbers off plots or re-quantifying gel images.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein sequences are obtainable from the two GenBank accessions and the mutations are written as residue substitutions, so inputs are recoverable - the only Part A item that is fine.

a4_units_stated.note: Activities are reported as relative amounts (percent of wild type) read from graphs; no units column exists because no table exists.

a5_enough_rows.note: About 25 single-point L-protein mutants were assayed (counted from mutation identifiers in the full text), versus the checklist minimum of ~400 for classification. Two orders of magnitude short.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Whatever exists is a PDF supplement; size is never the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked: no file was retrievable, so there is no download count to compare with the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would come from real radiolabelled enzyme assays (32-P gel quantification), not from another model's output - provenance is clean, there is just far too little of it.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is possible: with ~25 assayed mutants of a single viral protein, reported only as gel images, any model would be fitting noise.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence changes to predict whether a virus polymerase can still add the protective cap to its messenger RNA.
plain_idea.train_on: Single amino-acid substitutions in the respiratory syncytial virus large (L) protein, each paired with its measured capping activity; about 25 such mutants exist in this paper, verified by counting mutation names in the text.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a mutant retains mRNA-capping activity, with the true answer coming from radioactive (32-P) gel assays of purified L-plus-phosphoprotein complexes, quantified by the authors as percent of wild type.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Antiviral programmes targeting the capping enzyme (for example the JNJ-8003 compound studied here) would like to know which residue changes abolish capping or confer drug resistance; but 25 measurements cannot support that.

ml_idea: Considered: predict capping / RNA-synthesis-initiation competence of respiratory syncytial virus L-protein point mutants from sequence or structure embeddings (ESM-2, a protein language model), possibly pooled with earlier vesicular stomatitis and Sendai virus L mutagenesis studies. Dead on arrival at this paper: the measurements are gel images for ~25 mutants with no machine-readable table.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: Part A failed before any compute question mattered.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the mutants with a quantified activity value - about 25 from the full text, versus ~400 needed for classification. That single count kills it in five minutes.

verdict_reason: Mechanistic enzymology paper with no deposited data: ~25 point mutants scored as gel bands in figures, no table, no repository.
